justification: Assessment reported INVALID at line 0025, identifying exactly the ground-truth flaw: the proof silently assumes a one-to-one (distinct-representative) assignment of the n elements of S to the factors 1..n with each element divisible by its factor, which the cited 'unique multiple in j consecutive integers' lemma does not supply. Its witness (m=5, n=4, S={5,6,7,8}) is a different but valid instance of the same failure: 4 forces 8, 3 forces 6, leaving no even element for 2 (5 and 7 odd), so no valid matching exists while 4! = 24 still divides 1680. It also correctly notes the theorem itself remains true, matching the ground truth's framing.
